title: PullbackSectionsDiagram
statement:
Let $I$ be a preorder, $D:I^{op}\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ an inverse system
[def-pc-scheme], $c$ a cone with vertex $X$ and projections $f_i:X\to X_i$, $i_0\in I$,
$\Lambda$ a commutative ring, $G$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $(X_{i_0})_{et}$
[def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $V_0\to X_{i_0}$ an etale object
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Put $J=\{i\mid i_0\le i\}$ and write $a_i:X_i\to X_{i_0}$
for the transition morphisms. Set $S_i=(a_{i,*}a_i^{-1}G)(V_0)$ and
$T=(f_{i_0,*}f_{i_0}^{-1}G)(V_0)$, using the direct and inverse images
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For $i\le j$ let
$b_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$ be the transition, so $a_j=b_{ji}a_i$ in diagrammatic order.
Define $\mu_{ji}:S_i\to S_j$ to be, on $V_0$ sections, $a_{i,*}$ of the unit
of $b_{ji}^{-1}\dashv b_{ji,*}$ at $a_i^{-1}G$, followed by the direct-image
composition isomorphism and by $a_{j,*}$ of the inverse-image composition
isomorphism $b_{ji}^{-1}a_i^{-1}G\to a_j^{-1}G$
[lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. Define $\tau_i:S_i\to T$ by the
same formula using $f_i$ instead of $b_{ji}$ and the cone equation
$f_{i_0}=f_i a_i$. Then there exist a functor $F:J\to\Lambda\text{-Mod}$, a cocone
$B$ of $F$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and isomorphisms $e_i:F(i)\to S_i$ and
$e_B:B.pt\to T$ such that, for every $i\le j$,
$e_j F(i\to j)e_i^{-1}=\mu_{ji}$ and $e_B B_i e_i^{-1}=\tau_i$.
This asserts the canonical section diagram and cocone, without a colimit property.

proof.text: Define the stage objects S_i and the arrow maps mu by the displayed adjunction-unit formula. The unit equation for the left-adjoint comparison identifies the corrected composite unit with the unit for the composite morphism; it holds for ModuleCat-valued sheaves directly.

Naturality of the units and associativity of direct-image composition give mu_g mu_f = mu_(fg). The identity comparison cancels the identity unit, giving mu_id = id. These formulas hold before evaluation at V_0, and evaluation preserves them.

Use the same calculation with the cone projection and the cone equation to obtain tau_j mu_f = tau_i. The resulting functor and cocone have exactly the prescribed objects, so their object comparisons can be identity isomorphisms.
